title: Let the Other Person Save Face
coreMove: When someone is wrong or losing, hand them a dignified exit before you press your point

exampleSpecs.domain: a head chef telling a line cook he has been plating the special wrong all week in front of the Saturday-night crew
exampleSpecs.audience: a head chef who runs a busy kitchen and has to keep the cook coming back Monday
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a competent young cook quits over public embarrassment instead of fixing his plating
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chef pulls the cook into the walk-in and reframes the error as a recipe-card problem so the cook can correct without confessing

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional pharmacy manager who has to remove a long-tenured pharmacist from a store leadership role after a dispensing audit
exampleSpecs.audience: a regional manager who has known the pharmacist for fifteen years
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the pharmacist stays with the company in a role that uses her real strengths or walks out humiliated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager opens by naming, in the pharmacist's own words, what she has been best at, then offers the new role as a use of that strength rather than a demotion

exampleSpecs.domain: a piano teacher correcting an adult beginner who has been practicing a passage with the wrong fingering for a month
exampleSpecs.audience: a piano teacher whose student is a sixty-year-old retiree paying out of pocket
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the student keeps coming to lessons or quietly cancels because he feels foolish
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the teacher praises the steadiness the student already built before naming the fingering change, so the change feels like an upgrade rather than a verdict

exampleSpecs.domain: a county prosecutor offering a plea to a first-time defendant in front of his mother in the courtroom hallway
exampleSpecs.audience: a county prosecutor who knows the kid will see his neighbors at church on Sunday
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the young man takes the deal or fights a losing case to protect his pride
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the prosecutor frames the plea in language that lets the defendant accept responsibility without being branded in front of his mother

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice nurse correcting a grown daughter who has been giving her dying father the wrong dose because she misread the chart
exampleSpecs.audience: a hospice nurse on a home visit
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the daughter keeps caring for her father at home or collapses into guilt and hands him over to a facility
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse praises the daughter's vigilance, locates the error in the chart's handwriting rather than the daughter's care, and corrects the dose without ever making her say she was wrong

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school principal handling a teacher who sent a sharply worded email to a parent that has now reached the superintendent
exampleSpecs.audience: a principal who needs the teacher to write an apology that does not read as forced
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the teacher learns to write a different email next time or hardens into resentment and a union grievance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the principal walks through what the parent likely felt reading the email, lets the teacher arrive at the rewrite herself, and never makes her recant the original in writing
